data.name: Hayal
data.gender_notes: Hayal is used as a unisex name in Islamic naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Arabic root h-y-l, meaning 'to fly'. In Islamic context, represents the ability to envision and create in the mind, as well as a source of inspiration and creativity. The name Hayal carries the meaning “Imagination” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic, Urdu, Persian. Parents who choose Hayal usually hope their child will grow to embody imagination and live with faith, good character and purpose.

in_arabic.name: هيال
in_arabic.long_meaning: هيال هو اسم عربي يعكس الوهم أو الخيال أو الحلم، وله جذور في اللغة العربية القديمة، ويُستخدم في الثقافة الإسلامية لتعبير عن الأماني والرغبات، حيث يرمز إلى التطلع إلى المستقبل والتفاؤل

in_urdu.name: حیال
in_urdu.long_meaning: حیال ایک عربی نام ہے جو وہم یا خیال یا خواب کی عکاسی کرتا ہے، اور اس کی جڑیں قدیم عربی زبان میں ہیں، اور اسے مسلم ثقافت میں امنگوں اور خواہشوں کے اظہار کے لیے استعمال کیا جاتا ہے

in_hindi.name: हयाल
in_hindi.long_meaning: हयाल एक अरबी नाम है जो वहम या कल्पना या सपने को दर्शाता है, और इसकी जड़ें प्राचीन अरबी भाषा में हैं, और इसका उपयोग मुस्लिम संस्कृति में आशाओं और इच्छाओं की अभिव्यक्ति के लिए किया जाता है

data.cultural_impact: The name Hayal can be perceived as having a deep cultural impact as it reflects the dynamic and imaginative nature of the Arabic language. Hayal, as a term, inspires creative thinking and expression, and is often used to describe abstract ideas or dreams. In this sense, it can be seen as a cultural symbol of the imagination and its power to shape reality.
data.spiritual_significance: From a spiritual perspective, Hayal can represent the divine inspiration that guides and illuminates the human mind. In Islamic teachings, it is believed that God communicates with His creation through dreams and visions, providing guidance and wisdom. Therefore, the name Hayal can be seen as a reminder of the spiritual significance of the human imagination and its ability to connect us with the divine. Additionally, Hayal can also evoke the idea of the human soul as a flying spirit, free from earthly constraints and limitations.

historical_references.reference: Ibn al-Qayyim mentions a man named Hayal ibn Yahya al-Juhani in his book 'I'lam al-Muwaqqi'in', who was a famous ascetic and Sufi scholar from Juhana in the Hejaz. He died around 639 AH (1242 AD).

Al-Maqrizi, in his work 'Al-Khitat al-Masriyah fi Ahwal Muluk Misr', mentions a man named Hayal ibn Khalaf al-Qushayri, who was the chief judge of Egypt under Sultan Qutuz. He died around 667 AH (1269 AD).
